description:
In her talk, Refugees Are Not the Problem, Parisa Pirooz challenges the way refugees are too often treated as passive recipients of help rather than capable people with knowledge, experience and ideas of their own. Drawing on her time working with Syrian and Palestinian refugee women in Jordan, she reflects on the moment she realised they did not need to be taught how to work. They needed safety, agency and a voice in the decisions shaping their lives.

Parisa asks what society loses when refugees are excluded from the rooms where policies and solutions are created, and argues that meaningful change begins by listening to those living with the consequences. Parisa Pirooz is the founder and executive director of Creshendo, a global nonprofit that centers refugee-led design in integration, storytelling, and economic empowerment. The daughter of parents who fled the 1979 Iranian Revolution, she grew up with an intimate understanding of displacement, resilience, and the quiet burdens carr
title: Refugees are not the problem | Parisa Pirooz | TEDxWolverhampton

author: TEDx Talks
description: How can Roxbury - and neighborhoods like it - fight the steady the loss of its Black residents and the rising tides of gentrification and housing instability? What if new community development projects helped to achieve both goals? In this talk, Dianne Wilkerson proposes an innovative idea to slow gentrification, grow generational wealth, and create thriving, intergenerational communities. Dianne Wilkerson’s life is a story of triumph and challenges. She has been defying odds from the beginning as a daughter of the segregated south and the descendant of slaves. She gained a reputation early on for tackling the most difficult social, economic and political issues - from housing discrimination to predatory lending. In the State Senate, she established the Commission to Eliminate Racial and Ethnic Health Disparities and authored groundbreaking legislation on racial profiling, wrongful convictions, reproductive rights, and insurance equity. Wilkerson is a well sought-after speaker/adviser
title: Back to Black Roxbury: Creating a Cycle of Generational Wealth | Dianne Wilkerson | TEDxRoxbury

In order for this to happen, we, as a community, must create safe spaces and cultivate our young authors, actors, and filmmakers, because no one can write our stories like us. Reagan Massó is an honor student at Boston Latin Academy and a passionate writer, actor, and aspiring filmmaker. A dedicated storyteller both on stage and on the page, Reagan is committed to creating work that reflects authenticity and imagination. She is a published writer and has appeared in numerous theater productions. She is also currently writing her first book, a science fiction novel titled WILHELMINA. description: Amanda Noventa has the dream career many people wish for: she's a professional traveler. After more than a decade exploring some of the most remote places on the planet, she shares how travel creates the distance needed to question certainties, reconsider choices, and open space for unexpected transformations. Not a believer in the idea of "traveling to find yourself," she reveals why the deepest changes tend to happen precisely when we're not looking for them. Amanda Noventa is a professional traveler, writing for Brazil's leading outlets and building a community of women travelers who don't just want to survive the routine — they want to explore the world. description:
When Muzhda lost access to her education after Taliban takeover of Afghanistan, she faced a choice most of us never have to make: accept the closed door, or become the reason it opens for someone else. She chose the second.

That single decision became the seed of CodeGreen Afghanistan — an initiative that has since reached more than 2,000 girls, giving them the tools to keep learning when the systems around them said they couldn't. In this talk, Muzhda traces the line from one person's refusal to give up to a movement that now ripples across borders and generations.

Her story is a reminder that change rarely begins with a crowd. It begins with one person deciding to do something — and trusting that the ripple will carry further than they can see.

One action. One person. That's where it starts. Muzhda Akbari is an award-winning Afghan activist advocating for girls’ education, refugee rights, and gender equality. Founder of CodeGreenAfg, she’s empowered thousands of Afghan girls thro

author: TEDx Talks
description: Procurador federal, doutor e professor, Thiago parte do nascimento da filha Diana — que coincidiu com a chegada da IA generativa — para expor o "FOBO" (fear of becoming obsolete), o medo de ficar ultrapassado. Ele conta o choque de ver a IA atualizar em cinco minutos um livro técnico que levou a vida para dominar, transformando o conhecimento em commodity, e reúne dados alarmantes sobre o impacto no emprego. Sua resposta não é um atalho: numa era em que saber a resposta deixou de ser o ponto, o que importa é o aprendizado real e a "transferência" — pegar o conhecimento e resolver problemas concretos, algo que exige esforço, leitura e pensamento. Ele mapeia quatro etapas para usar bem a IA (delegação, descrição, discernimento e diligência) e conclui que a habilidade decisiva é "aprender a aprender, e aprender com velocidade". Thiago Murilo Nóbrega Galvão é Procurador Federal desde 2011 e atualmente exerce a função de Procurador-Chefe Federal junto ao IFRN, em Natal/RN. Doutor em Direit
title: Como aprender num mundo em que a máquina já sabe a resposta? | Thiago Nóbrega | TEDxPipa

Every iteration of our life blueprint is not final. It is always a draft. Guided by this philosophy, Gandhi shares how our blueprints of life need not to conform to limiting expectations, but are rather shaped by our decisions, interests and passions. Gandhi started his own litigation firm because he believed that legal representation needs to be personal, strategic and built around the client. A decade in the courtroom has taught him that winning isn't all about knowing the law, but preparation, clear thinking and the willingness to fight for the right outcome.

Beyond the courtroom, Gandhi is also a certified trainer who runs his own human resources training firm, Mindspire Training & Consultancy. He focuses on corporate programmes related to workplace bullying, sexual harassment, contract litigacy and defamation. title: You are Not the Blueprint they Handed You | Gandhi Palanisamy | TEDxPOWIIS Youth

Jeremy McKane, an ocean artist and technologist, highlights the disconnect between the ecological value of our oceans and how they are recorded in global economic systems. Focusing on seagrass meadows—which are vital for carbon capture yet often valued at zero—he demonstrates how modern technology like satellite data, sensors, and AI can provide the "receipts" needed to verify nature’s worth. He shares how this approach creates a bridge between finance and the living world, transforming nature from an overlooked resource into a verifiable asset.
 Jeremy McKane’s passion for the environment is at the core of his work as an artist and entrepreneur. When he is not underwater taking photographs, he can be found on land, as CEO of OCN.ai. Born from his commitment to the ocean, OCN.ai creates technology to monitor the health of the ocean and create trackable solutions for a regenerative economy. Sam Weber is an adventurer, leader, and business strategist who rowed 3,000 miles across the Atlantic Ocean in 53 days.
